questions.stem: Bihu is the most important festival and dance form of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Bihu is Assam's principal festival, celebrated in three forms each year: (1) RONGALI/BOHAG BIHU (April, New Year, spring harvest) — the biggest, with the vibrant Bihu dance; (2) KONGALI/KATI BIHU (October, bereft, austere — diyas lit in paddy fields); (3) BHOGALI/MAGH BIHU (January, harvest, community feasting). The Bihu dance features high-energy hip movements, 'pepa' (buffalo horn flute), 'dhol' (drum), 'gogona' (reed instrument).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Hornbill Festival, a vibrant showcase of tribal culture, is celebrated every December in which state?
questions.explanation: The Hornbill Festival is held every year 1-10 December at Kisama Heritage Village near Kohima, Nagaland. Named after the Indian hornbill bird revered by Naga tribes. Showcases all 17 recognised Naga tribes (Ao, Angami, Konyak, Lotha, Sema, Chakhesang, Rengma, etc.) — their dances, music, traditional sports (Naga wrestling), handicrafts, and cuisine. Started in 2000 by the State Government to promote inter-tribal interaction. Often called the 'Festival of Festivals'.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Chapchar Kut, a spring festival marking the end of jungle-clearing for jhum cultivation, is celebrated in which state?
questions.explanation: Chapchar Kut is the most important festival of the Mizo people of Mizoram, celebrated in March after the jungle clearing ('jhum' or slash-and-burn) phase for the new planting season. Features the famous CHERAW (Bamboo Dance) — performed by women stepping between bamboo poles clapped in rhythm by men. Also includes Khuallam, Sarlamkai, Solakia, Chheihlam dances. Other Mizo festivals: Mim Kut (maize harvest, Aug-Sept), Pawl Kut (winter harvest, Dec-Jan).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Nongkrem is the most important religious festival of which tribal community of which state?
questions.explanation: Nongkrem is the 5-day harvest thanksgiving festival of the Khasi people of Meghalaya, held in November at Smit, Khasi Hills — the seat of the Syiem (traditional head). Features the sacred Pomblang ritual (goat sacrifice) and the Nongkrem dance — unmarried women in traditional dress with gold ornaments dance in a circle while men with swords and flywhisks dance around them. The Garos' corresponding major festival is WANGALA ('100 Drums Festival') in November, post-harvest. Apatani: Dree festival.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Losoong (also called Sonam Lochar) is the new year harvest festival of which Sikkimese community?
questions.explanation: Losoong (Tibetan New Year / harvest festival) is celebrated by the Bhutia community of Sikkim in December (10th month of Tibetan calendar). The similar Namsoong is celebrated by the Lepcha community. Saga Dawa (May-June) commemorates Buddha's birth, enlightenment, and parinirvana — observed by all Sikkimese Buddhists. Other Sikkim festivals: Tihar/Diwali (Nepali), Bhumchu (water festival at Tashiding monastery), Pang Lhabsol (Mt Khangchendzonga worship).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Lai Haraoba and Ras Leela are the traditional dance-drama forms of which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Lai Haraoba ('Merry-making of the gods') is the oldest ritual dance of Manipur, predating Vaishnavism, honouring the indigenous Meitei deities (Umang Lai). Manipuri Ras Leela, developed under King Bhagyachandra (18th c.), depicts Radha-Krishna's divine love. Manipuri is one of the 8 classical dances of India — characterised by graceful, gentle movements, unique ball-shaped 'pung' drum accompaniment, and elaborate skirted 'Kumil' costumes (the female dancer moves almost like a spinning top).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Bagurumba is a famous butterfly-mimic folk dance of which community of Assam?
questions.explanation: Bagurumba (the 'Butterfly Dance') is the signature folk dance of the Bodo tribal community of Assam and parts of NE. Performed primarily by women during festivals (especially Baisagu — the Bodo new year in April), with graceful wing-like arm movements imitating butterflies. Accompanying instruments: Kham (drum), Siphung (flute), Serja (violin-like), Jotha (cymbals). Other Assamese tribal dances: Ali Ai Ligang (Mishing spring dance), Rongker (Karbi), Baidima (Dimasa).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Solung, Mopin, and Dree are festivals of different tribes in which state?
questions.explanation: Arunachal has 26 major tribes, each with its own festival: SOLUNG (Adi tribe — Aug-Sept, agricultural), MOPIN (Galo tribe — April, harvest, rice powder smearing), DREE (Apatani tribe — July, agricultural thanksgiving), LOSAR (Monpa, Sherdukpen Buddhist — Feb), NYOKUM (Nyishi tribe — Feb, earth goddess), BOORI BOOT (Hill Miris — Feb), REH (Idu Mishmi). Arunachal is the land of 'dawn-lit mountains'; its tribes speak over 50 languages/dialects.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Garia and Hojagiri are popular folk dances of which NE state?
questions.explanation: GARIA is a Tripura folk dance of the Tripuri community celebrating the deity Garia (god of wealth/fertility) during the April Garia Puja festival — dancers form a chain around a bamboo pole. HOJAGIRI is the acrobatic dance of the Reang (Bru) tribe — women balance on earthen pitchers while performing intricate upper-body movements with bottles/lamps on their head (one of India's most visually distinctive dances). Bizu (end-of-Chaitra festival) is the Chakma community's equivalent.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Ghoomar, Kalbeliya, and Terah Tali are traditional folk dances of which state?
questions.explanation: GHOOMAR: graceful women's dance in flowing ghaghra, originally Bhil then adopted by royal Rajput courts (gained global fame via 2018 Padmaavat film). KALBELIYA: the 'Snake Charmer Dance' of the Kalbeliya (Sapera) nomadic community — UNESCO Intangible Heritage (2010); fluid twirling movements in black swirling skirts. TERAH TALI: a sit-down dance of the Kamad community for Baba Ramdev, where women strike 13 tiny cymbals tied to their bodies. Other Rajasthani: Gair (men), Chakri, Bhavai (balancing pots), Kachhi Ghodi (mock horse).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Chhau is a semi-classical dance form performed in which three states?
questions.explanation: Chhau, inscribed on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list in 2010, has three distinct schools: (1) PURULIA CHHAU (West Bengal — most ornate, big colorful masks); (2) SERAIKELLA CHHAU (Jharkhand — masks, refined movements); (3) MAYURBHANJ CHHAU (Odisha — NO masks, most acrobatic/martial). Themes are from Ramayana, Mahabharata, tribal lore. Performed primarily during the Chaitra Parva festival in spring. Roots in martial arts (Phari-Khanda) and tribal dance.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Theyyam, a ritualistic dance where the performer embodies a deity, is performed in which state?
questions.explanation: Theyyam (also Kaliyattam, Tira) is a sacred ritual dance-drama of North Malabar (Kannur, Kasaragod districts) of Kerala. Over 400 distinct Theyyam forms exist; the performer, after elaborate makeup and costume (often spanning 8-10 hours to don), is believed to become the deity itself — devotees seek blessings directly from 'the god'. Associated with Kaavu (sacred groves) and the Dravidian pre-Hindu pantheon. Other Kerala dances: Kathakali (classical), Mohiniyattam (classical), Padayani, Koodiyattam (UNESCO 2001), Ottamthullal.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Lavani and Tamasha are folk performing arts most associated with which state?
questions.explanation: LAVANI is Maharashtra's famous women's dance performed to the beats of the Dholki drum; 'lavanya' means beauty. Popularised during 18th-19th c. Peshwa era; often features in Tamasha. TAMASHA is the popular folk-theatre form of Maharashtra combining dance, drama, and music, traditionally performed by the Kolhati and Mahar communities. Other Maharashtra folk: Gondhal (ritual dance-song for Devi), Lezim (martial stick dance), Dhangari Gaja (shepherd tribe), Povadas (heroic ballads on Shivaji).
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: The Konyak tribe's Aoling festival and the Ao tribe's Moatsu Mong are celebrated in which state?
questions.explanation: Nagaland has 17 recognised tribes, each with signature festivals: AOLING (Konyaks — April, spring, new year); MOATSU MONG (Aos — May, post-sowing); TULUNI (Sumis — July, abundance); SEKRENYI (Angamis — Feb, purification); TOKHU EMONG (Lothas — Nov, post-harvest); BUSHU JIBA (Kacharis); NGADA (Rengmas); MIMKUT (not to be confused with Mizo — Kukis have one too). Konyaks are historically known as the 'Headhunter' tribe (the practice ceased 1960s). Know at least 5-6 tribe-festival pairings.
questions.subject: General Knowledge

questions.stem: Which of the following is the harvest festival celebrated in Tamil Nadu in January?
questions.explanation: PONGAL is Tamil Nadu's 4-day harvest festival in mid-January (Thai month): Day 1 BHOGI (discarding old), Day 2 THAI (Surya) PONGAL (cooking the Pongal dish — sweet rice overflowing the pot signals prosperity), Day 3 MATTU PONGAL (honouring cattle), Day 4 KAANUM PONGAL (family reunion). Coincides with Makar Sankranti / Lohri (Punjab) / Uttarayan (Guj) / Magh Bihu (Assam) / Pedda Panduga (AP). Onam = Kerala (Aug-Sept Malayalam new year harvest). Ugadi = Karnataka/AP/Telangana (Chaitra new year).
